```{r}
#| label: annotation-load
df <- read.csv(here("data/references.csv"), na.strings = "") %>%
  select(-any_of(c("annotations_cite_key", "annotations_id", "entry_type", "authors", "year", "title", "venue", "pages", "doi", "bibliography_json_key")))

df <- df %>%
  mutate(publication_year = as.numeric(str_extract_all(citekey, "\\d+")))

df$publication_year <- factor(df$publication_year,
                              levels = as.character(seq(min(df$publication_year,
                                       na.rm = TRUE),
                                       max(df$publication_year, na.rm = TRUE), 1)))

# Exported so 03_joined_descriptions.qmd can load it when rendered
# standalone (outside the combined index.qmd include chain), without
# recomputing Part 1 — consistent with 03's own stated design ("does
# not recompute either" upstream part).
write_csv(df, here("analysis", "bibvik_annotation_df.csv"))
```

```{r}
#| label: annotation-shared-helpers
# Shared across every "by year" and Wilson-faded chart in this
# document (Gender, Topic, Method, Source of Evidence) -- defined once
# here so all of them draw on the same functions and the same
# per-year paper counts.
wilson_lower_bound <- function(x, n, conf = 0.95) {
  z <- qnorm(1 - (1 - conf) / 2)
  phat <- x / n
  denom <- 1 + z^2 / n
  centre <- phat + z^2 / (2 * n)
  adj <- z * sqrt(phat * (1 - phat) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))
  (centre - adj) / denom
}
wilson_upper_bound <- function(x, n, conf = 0.95) {
  z <- qnorm(1 - (1 - conf) / 2)
  phat <- x / n
  denom <- 1 + z^2 / n
  centre <- phat + z^2 / (2 * n)
  adj <- z * sqrt(phat * (1 - phat) / n + z^2 / (4 * n^2))
  (centre + adj) / denom
}

# Base-R centered rolling sum (window of 3, shrinking at the edges to
# whatever's available rather than requiring a full window) -- avoids
# adding a package dependency (slider) for one small operation.
roll_sum3 <- function(x) {
  n <- length(x)
  vapply(seq_len(n), function(i) sum(x[max(1, i - 1):min(n, i + 1)]), numeric(1))
}

# Tables that sit beside the plots, in a Plot / Table tabset. Each takes
# the object its plot already built, so a table holds exactly the numbers
# the plot draws. Shares are rounded for reading; the Wilson columns are
# the same 95% interval the faded bars use. `group` is the name of the
# grouping column ("topic", "method", "source" or "region").
as_pct <- function(x, digits = 1) round(100 * x, digits)

# Per group and year: counts, share, enrichment and the Wilson interval.
# Years with no papers have no share and are dropped.
year_wilson_table <- function(d, group) {
  d %>%
    filter(!is.na(n_papers_year)) %>%
    arrange(.data[[group]], publication_year) %>%
    select(all_of(group), year = publication_year, papers = n,
           `papers that year` = n_papers_year, share = prop, enrichment,
           low = ci_lower, high = ci_upper) %>%
    mutate(share = as_pct(share), enrichment = round(enrichment, 2),
           low = as_pct(low), high = as_pct(high)) %>%
    rename(`share (%)` = share, `Wilson 95% low (%)` = low,
           `Wilson 95% high (%)` = high)
}

# The same, for the 3-year rolling window behind the smoothed trend. The
# interval is on the pooled counts and is in enrichment units, as plotted.
year_roll_table <- function(d, group) {
  d %>%
    filter(!is.na(n_papers_year)) %>%
    arrange(.data[[group]], publication_year) %>%
    select(all_of(group), year = publication_year,
           `papers in window` = roll_n, `all papers in window` = roll_n_papers_year,
           `smoothed enrichment` = roll_enrichment,
           low = roll_ci_lower, high = roll_ci_upper) %>%
    mutate(across(c(`smoothed enrichment`, low, high), ~ round(., 2))) %>%
    rename(`Wilson 95% low (enrichment)` = low, `Wilson 95% high (enrichment)` = high)
}

# First-author gender within each group. Top row = top bar of the plot.
gender_first_author_table <- function(merged, group) {
  merged %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(group))) %>%
    summarise(papers = sum(n),
              `woman first` = sum(n[gender_first_author %in% "Woman"]),
              `man first` = sum(n[gender_first_author %in% "Man"]),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(`other or missing` = papers - `woman first` - `man first`,
           `% woman first` = as_pct(`woman first` / papers),
           `Wilson 95% low (%)` = as_pct(wilson_lower_bound(`woman first`, papers)),
           `Wilson 95% high (%)` = as_pct(wilson_upper_bound(`woman first`, papers))) %>%
    arrange(desc(`% woman first`)) %>%
    select(all_of(group), papers, `woman first`, `man first`, `other or missing`,
           `% woman first`, `Wilson 95% low (%)`, `Wilson 95% high (%)`)
}

# Author-list gender composition within each group, as n (share of the
# group's papers). Rows run from the largest female share down, as the
# plot's bars run from the top.
gender_composition_table <- function(comp_summary, female_share, group) {
  groups5 <- c("solo-female", "all-female (multi-author)", "mixed",
               "all-male (multi-author)", "solo-male")
  comp_summary %>%
    mutate(composition = if_else(composition_singleauthor_split %in% groups5,
                                 composition_singleauthor_split, "uncertain")) %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(c(group, "total", "composition")))) %>%
    summarise(n = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(cell = paste0(n, " (", round(100 * n / total), "%)")) %>%
    select(-n) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = composition, values_from = cell, values_fill = "0 (0%)") %>%
    left_join(female_share, by = group) %>%
    mutate(female_share = replace_na(female_share, 0)) %>%
    arrange(desc(female_share)) %>%
    select(all_of(group), papers = total, any_of(c(groups5, "uncertain")))
}

# Mixed-gender papers only: how many have a woman first author, and how
# large the author teams are.
gender_mixed_table <- function(raw, group) {
  raw %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(group))) %>%
    summarise(`mixed papers` = n(), `woman first` = sum(is_woman_first),
              `median team size` = median(n_authors),
              `smallest team` = min(n_authors), `largest team` = max(n_authors),
              .groups = "drop") %>%
    mutate(`% woman first` = as_pct(`woman first` / `mixed papers`),
           `Wilson 95% low (%)` = as_pct(wilson_lower_bound(`woman first`, `mixed papers`)),
           `Wilson 95% high (%)` = as_pct(wilson_upper_bound(`woman first`, `mixed papers`))) %>%
    arrange(desc(`% woman first`)) %>%
    select(all_of(group), `mixed papers`, `woman first`, `% woman first`,
           `Wilson 95% low (%)`, `Wilson 95% high (%)`,
           `median team size`, `smallest team`, `largest team`)
}

# Enrichment heatmaps: one row per cell of the heatmap, from the top row of the
# heatmap down and, within a row, from the most enriched category. `row` and
# `category` are the heatmap's column names; `row_papers` and `baseline` name
# the columns holding the row's paper count and the rate enrichment divides by.
enrichment_cell_table <- function(d, row, row_name, category, row_papers, baseline) {
  out <- d %>%
    arrange(desc(as.integer(.data[[row]])), desc(enrichment), .data[[category]]) %>%
    transmute(c1 = as.character(.data[[row]]), c2 = .data[[category]],
              papers = n, `papers in row` = .data[[row_papers]],
              `share (%)` = as_pct(prop), `baseline rate (%)` = as_pct(.data[[baseline]]),
              enrichment = round(enrichment, 2))
  names(out)[1:2] <- c(row_name, category)
  out
}

n_per_year <- df %>% count(publication_year, name = "n_papers_year")
n_total_papers <- n_distinct(df$citekey)
```

## Gender

Author gender, examined two ways: first-author gender and all-author
gender by year, and gender composition across the full author list per
paper.

### By year

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: gender-by-year
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Top: first author only, one bar per gender per year — faint bars
#|   mean few papers published that year. Bottom: every author
#|   position pooled (order not preserved), so a multi-author paper
#|   contributes more than one tally — faint bars there mean few
#|   author-slots that year, not few papers. Same Wilson-interval fade
#|   used throughout this document, computed against the relevant
#|   denominator for each panel.
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
gender_pubyears <- df %>%
  count(publication_year, Authors..Genders..Author.1., name = "n") %>%
  left_join(n_per_year, by = "publication_year") %>%
  mutate(
    ci_lower = wilson_lower_bound(n, n_papers_year),
    ci_upper = wilson_upper_bound(n, n_papers_year),
    ci_width = ci_upper - ci_lower
  )

plt1 <-
ggplot(data = gender_pubyears, aes(x = publication_year, y = n, fill = Authors..Genders..Author.1., alpha = -ci_width)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", position = 'dodge') +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = gender_colors) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = seq(2000, 2022, 1), drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Count", fill = "First author gender", title = "First author gender by year") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

all_authors_gender_year <- df %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Authors.."),
    names_to  = "position",
    values_to = "gender"
  ) %>%
  mutate(gender = na_if(gender, "")) %>%
  drop_na(gender) %>%
  count(publication_year, gender)

# Denominator here is total author-slots that year, not paper count --
# a multi-author paper contributes more than one gender tally, so
# pooled counts routinely exceed n_papers_year and phat = n/n_papers_year
# would exceed 1, which breaks the Wilson formula (undefined variance).
n_author_slots_per_year <- all_authors_gender_year %>%
  group_by(publication_year) %>%
  summarise(n_slots_year = sum(n), .groups = "drop")

all_authors_gender_year <- all_authors_gender_year %>%
  left_join(n_author_slots_per_year, by = "publication_year") %>%
  mutate(
    ci_lower = wilson_lower_bound(n, n_slots_year),
    ci_upper = wilson_upper_bound(n, n_slots_year),
    ci_width = ci_upper - ci_lower
  )

plt2 <-
ggplot(data = all_authors_gender_year, aes(x = publication_year, y = n, fill = gender, alpha = -ci_width)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", position = 'dodge') +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = nord_palettes$victory_bonds[c(3, 1, 4)]) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), guide = "none") +
  scale_x_discrete(breaks = seq(2000, 2022, 1), drop = FALSE) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Count", fill = "Author gender", title = "All authors' gender by year") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

plt1 / plt2
```

#### Table, first author

The top panel's numbers. The share and interval use all papers published that year as the denominator.

```{r}
#| label: gender-by-year-table-first
knitr::kable(
gender_pubyears %>%
  arrange(publication_year, Authors..Genders..Author.1.) %>%
  select(year = publication_year, `first author gender` = Authors..Genders..Author.1.,
         papers = n, `papers that year` = n_papers_year, ci_lower, ci_upper) %>%
  mutate(`share (%)` = as_pct(papers / `papers that year`),
         `Wilson 95% low (%)` = as_pct(ci_lower),
         `Wilson 95% high (%)` = as_pct(ci_upper)) %>%
  select(-ci_lower, -ci_upper)
)
```

#### Table, all authors

The bottom panel's numbers. The denominator is the author slots that year, not the papers.

```{r}
#| label: gender-by-year-table-all
knitr::kable(
all_authors_gender_year %>%
  arrange(publication_year, gender) %>%
  select(year = publication_year, gender, `author slots` = n,
         `author slots that year` = n_slots_year, ci_lower, ci_upper) %>%
  mutate(`share (%)` = as_pct(`author slots` / `author slots that year`),
         `Wilson 95% low (%)` = as_pct(ci_lower),
         `Wilson 95% high (%)` = as_pct(ci_upper)) %>%
  select(-ci_lower, -ci_upper)
)
```

:::

### Composition across the full author list

First-author gender and the order-blind pool above don't capture gender
**composition per paper** (all-male vs. all-female vs. mixed) or **order**
within a paper.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: gender-sequence
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3
author_gender_cols <- df %>%
  select(starts_with("Authors..Genders..Author.")) %>%
  names()

# Per-paper ordered gender sequence (e.g. "Man, Woman, Man"), preserving
# author order and author count, rather than pooling into an unordered set.
gender_sequences <- df %>%
  select(citekey, all_of(author_gender_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(author_gender_cols),
    names_to = "position",
    values_to = "gender"
  ) %>%
  mutate(gender = na_if(gender, "")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gender)) %>%
  # Extract numeric author position from the column name for correct
  # ordering regardless of how many positions exist.
  mutate(author_n = as.integer(str_extract(position, "\\d+$"))) %>%
  arrange(citekey, author_n) %>%
  group_by(citekey) %>%
  summarise(
    n_authors        = n(),
    gender_sequence  = paste(gender, collapse = ", "),
    first_author_gender = first(gender),
    last_author_gender  = last(gender),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

gender_sequences |>
  count(n_authors) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(n_authors), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = topic_col) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.3, size = 3.5) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.15))) +
  labs(x = "Authors per paper", y = "Papers") +
  theme_bw()
```

#### Table

The plot's numbers.

```{r}
#| label: gender-sequence-table
knitr::kable(
gender_sequences %>%
  count(`authors per paper` = n_authors, name = "papers") %>%
  mutate(`% of papers` = as_pct(papers / sum(papers)))
)
```

:::

Several ways of collapsing a per-paper gender sequence into a single
cross-tabbable category are compared below — a strict all-same-vs-mixed
split, a majority-based split, and a version that separates solo
authorship out from multi-author teams (since "all-male" means something
different for n=1 than for a genuinely uniform team).

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: gender-composition-candidates
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5
composition_candidates <- gender_sequences %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(
    genders_list = list(str_split(gender_sequence, ", ")[[1]]),
    n_men       = sum(genders_list == "Man"),
    n_women     = sum(genders_list == "Woman"),
    n_uncertain = sum(genders_list == "Uncertain"),
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    # Strict: all-same vs. mixed
    composition_strict = case_when(
      n_uncertain > 0            ~ "includes uncertain",
      n_men > 0 & n_women == 0   ~ "all-male",
      n_women > 0 & n_men == 0   ~ "all-female",
      n_men > 0 & n_women > 0    ~ "mixed",
      TRUE                       ~ NA_character_
    ),
    # Majority-based (ties = balanced)
    composition_majority = case_when(
      n_uncertain > 0     ~ "includes uncertain",
      n_men > n_women     ~ "majority-male",
      n_women > n_men     ~ "majority-female",
      n_men == n_women    ~ "balanced",
      TRUE                ~ NA_character_
    ),
    # Single-author papers split out separately, since "all-male"/
    # "all-female" for n=1 is a different phenomenon than for n>1
    composition_singleauthor_split = case_when(
      n_authors == 1 & n_men == 1   ~ "solo-male",
      n_authors == 1 & n_women == 1 ~ "solo-female",
      n_authors == 1                ~ "solo-uncertain",
      n_uncertain > 0                ~ "includes uncertain",
      n_men > 0 & n_women == 0       ~ "all-male (multi-author)",
      n_women > 0 & n_men == 0       ~ "all-female (multi-author)",
      TRUE                           ~ "mixed"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(-genders_list)

bind_rows(
  composition_candidates |> count(value = composition_strict) |> mutate(scheme = "Strict"),
  composition_candidates |> count(value = composition_majority) |> mutate(scheme = "Majority"),
  composition_candidates |> count(value = composition_singleauthor_split) |> mutate(scheme = "Solo split out")
) |>
  mutate(scheme = factor(scheme, levels = c("Strict", "Majority", "Solo split out"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(value, n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = topic_col) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(vars(scheme), scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Papers") +
  theme_bw()
```

#### Table

The plot's numbers, one block per scheme.

```{r}
#| label: gender-composition-candidates-table
knitr::kable(
bind_rows(
  composition_candidates |> count(value = composition_strict) |> mutate(scheme = "Strict"),
  composition_candidates |> count(value = composition_majority) |> mutate(scheme = "Majority"),
  composition_candidates |> count(value = composition_singleauthor_split) |> mutate(scheme = "Solo split out")
) %>%
  mutate(scheme = factor(scheme, levels = c("Strict", "Majority", "Solo split out"))) %>%
  group_by(scheme) %>%
  arrange(scheme, desc(n)) %>%
  mutate(`% of papers` = as_pct(n / sum(n))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(scheme, category = value, papers = n, `% of papers`)
)
```

:::

### Gender over time

The first-author and all-author charts above count genders per year. This section turns them into shares of each year's papers. Bars are the share for one year, faded when few papers were published that year. The line is a 3-year rolling share and the band is its Wilson 95% interval on the pooled counts. The dashed line is the share across the whole corpus. Early years hold only a handful of papers each, so read the line and the band before any single bar.

```{r}
#| label: gender-trend-setup
# One row per paper, from the objects built above.
paper_traits <- composition_candidates %>%
  select(citekey, n_authors, composition = composition_singleauthor_split) %>%
  left_join(df %>% select(citekey, publication_year), by = "citekey")

# Per series and year: papers with the trait, their share of that year's
# papers and its Wilson interval, and the same on a 3-year pooled window.
# `counts` has one row per series and year, with every year present.
share_trend <- function(counts) {
  counts %>%
    left_join(n_per_year, by = "publication_year") %>%
    arrange(series, publication_year) %>%
    group_by(series) %>%
    mutate(share = n / n_papers_year,
           corpus_share = sum(n) / sum(n_papers_year),
           ci_lower = wilson_lower_bound(n, n_papers_year),
           ci_upper = wilson_upper_bound(n, n_papers_year),
           ci_width = ci_upper - ci_lower,
           roll_n = roll_sum3(n),
           roll_n_papers_year = roll_sum3(n_papers_year),
           roll_share = roll_n / roll_n_papers_year,
           roll_ci_lower = wilson_lower_bound(roll_n, roll_n_papers_year),
           roll_ci_upper = wilson_upper_bound(roll_n, roll_n_papers_year)) %>%
    ungroup()
}

share_trend_plot <- function(d, fill, ylab, ncol = 1, free_y = FALSE) {
  ggplot(d, aes(x = publication_year)) +
    geom_col(aes(y = share, alpha = -ci_width), fill = fill) +
    geom_hline(aes(yintercept = corpus_share), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
    geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = roll_ci_lower, ymax = roll_ci_upper, group = series),
                fill = trend_col, alpha = 0.18) +
    geom_line(aes(y = roll_share, group = series), colour = trend_col, linewidth = 0.8) +
    facet_wrap(~ series, ncol = ncol, scales = if (free_y) "free_y" else "fixed") +
    scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), guide = "none") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = "", y = ylab) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1))
}

# `count_name` heads the column of papers with the trait. `series_name` heads
# the series column, or drops it when there is only one series.
share_trend_table <- function(d, count_name, series_name = NULL) {
  out <- d %>%
    transmute(series, year = publication_year, papers = n, `papers that year` = n_papers_year,
              `share (%)` = as_pct(share),
              `Wilson 95% low (%)` = as_pct(ci_lower), `Wilson 95% high (%)` = as_pct(ci_upper),
              `papers in window` = roll_n, `all papers in window` = roll_n_papers_year,
              `smoothed share (%)` = as_pct(roll_share),
              `smoothed Wilson 95% low (%)` = as_pct(roll_ci_lower),
              `smoothed Wilson 95% high (%)` = as_pct(roll_ci_upper))
  names(out)[names(out) == "papers"] <- count_name
  if (is.null(series_name)) return(select(out, -series))
  names(out)[names(out) == "series"] <- series_name
  out
}

woman_first_trend <- df %>%
  group_by(publication_year) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(Authors..Genders..Author.1. %in% "Woman"), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(series = "Woman first author") %>%
  share_trend()

composition_levels <- c("solo-female", "solo-male", "all-female (multi-author)",
                        "all-male (multi-author)", "mixed", "uncertain")
composition_trend <- paper_traits %>%
  mutate(series = factor(if_else(composition %in% composition_levels[1:5], composition, "uncertain"),
                         levels = composition_levels)) %>%
  count(publication_year, series, name = "n") %>%
  complete(publication_year, series, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  group_by(series) %>%
  filter(sum(n) > 0) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(series = droplevels(series)) %>%
  share_trend()
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### First author

```{r}
#| label: gender-trend-first-author
#| fig-cap: "Share of each year's papers with a woman first author. Faint bars: few papers that year. Line and band: 3-year rolling share with its Wilson 95% interval. Dashed: share across the corpus."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5
share_trend_plot(woman_first_trend, gender_colors[["Woman"]], "Papers with a woman first author")
```

#### Author-list composition


### Team size over time

Authors per paper counted from the same author lists. The chart shows the share of each year's papers with two or more authors. The median is 1 in most years, so it would plot flat. The table adds the median and mean authors per paper. Bars, line, band and dashed line are read as in the section above.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: team-size-trend
#| fig-cap: "Share of each year's papers with two or more authors. Faint bars: few papers that year. Line and band: 3-year rolling share with its Wilson 95% interval. Dashed: share across the corpus."
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 3.5
team_size_trend <- paper_traits %>%
  group_by(publication_year) %>%
  summarise(n = sum(n_authors >= 2), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(series = "Two or more authors") %>%
  share_trend()

share_trend_plot(team_size_trend, nord_palettes$victory_bonds[1], "Papers with two or more authors")
```

#### Table

The chart's numbers: one row per year, with the median and mean authors per paper added.

```{r}
#| label: team-size-trend-table
knitr::kable(
share_trend_table(team_size_trend, "two or more authors") %>%
  left_join(paper_traits %>%
              group_by(year = publication_year) %>%
              summarise(`median authors` = median(n_authors),
                        `mean authors` = round(mean(n_authors), 2),
                        .groups = "drop"),
            by = "year")
)
```

## Topic

A paper can carry a Primary-coded topic (the coder's judgment of its main
focus) and any number of Secondary-coded topics (also present, but not
the main focus) — see the codebook for the exact scope of each topic
category. Charts below count a paper toward a topic if it carries either
value, so a paper coded with one Primary and two Secondary topics
contributes to three bars — counts and proportions are not mutually
exclusive across topics and will not sum to the corpus total. This
applies throughout this document, not just to Topic.

```{r}
#| label: topics-setup
topic_count <- df %>%
  select(publication_year, contains("Topics")) %>%
  pivot_longer(!publication_year,
               names_to = "topic",
               values_to = "count")

totals_by_year <- df %>%
  count(publication_year) %>%
  rename(total = n)
```

### Totals

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: topics-totals
#| fig-cap: >
#|   A paper counts toward a topic once, regardless of how many values
#|   it carries (Primary or Secondary — see above).
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
merged_count <- topic_count %>%
  filter(!is.na(count)) %>%
  mutate(topic = str_replace_all(str_remove(topic, "Topics.."), fixed("."), " ")) %>%
  count(topic) %>%
  mutate(pct = n / sum(n))

ggplot(merged_count, aes(x = reorder(str_wrap(topic, width = 25), n), y = n)) +
  geom_col(fill = topic_col) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))) +
  labs(x = "Topic", y = "Count") +
  theme_bw() +
  coord_flip()
ggsave("topics_aggregate.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 8, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

#### Table

The plot's numbers, with each count as a share of all papers in the corpus.

```{r}
#| label: topics-totals-table
knitr::kable(
merged_count %>%
  arrange(desc(n), topic) %>%
  transmute(topic, papers = n, `% of papers` = as_pct(n / n_total_papers))
)
```

:::

### Over time

```{r}
#| label: topics-over-time-setup
# Built directly from df (not topic_count above, which was pivoted
# without citekey and can't be used to count distinct papers per topic).
topic_long_with_key <- df %>%
  select(citekey, publication_year, contains("Topics")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = contains("Topics"), names_to = "topic", values_to = "count") %>%
  filter(!is.na(count)) %>%
  mutate(topic = str_replace_all(str_remove(topic, "Topics.."), fixed("."), " "))

topic_corpus_rate <- topic_long_with_key %>%
  distinct(citekey, topic) %>%
  count(topic, name = "n_corpus") %>%
  mutate(corpus_rate = n_corpus / n_total_papers)

topic_year_wilson <- topic_long_with_key %>%
  distinct(citekey, publication_year, topic) %>%
  count(publication_year, topic, name = "n") %>%
  complete(publication_year, topic, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  left_join(n_per_year, by = "publication_year") %>%
  left_join(topic_corpus_rate, by = "topic") %>%
  mutate(
    prop = n / n_papers_year,
    enrichment = prop / corpus_rate,
    ci_lower = wilson_lower_bound(n, n_papers_year),
    ci_upper = wilson_upper_bound(n, n_papers_year),
    ci_width = ci_upper - ci_lower
  ) %>%
  arrange(topic, publication_year)

# Rolling: pool counts over a 3-year window, then compute the Wilson CI
# on the POOLED proportion directly (not by averaging per-year CIs).
# ylim(0,4) on the enrichment charts below clips extreme ratios that
# come from topics with a very low corpus_rate (e.g. Heritage)
# inflating the enrichment-scaled interval -- clipping is done
# per-panel via coord_cartesian, not via a shared alpha scale, so one
# topic's wide interval cannot distort the visual reading of every
# other topic's panel.
topic_year_roll <- topic_year_wilson %>%
  arrange(topic, publication_year) %>%
  group_by(topic) %>%
  mutate(
    roll_n = roll_sum3(n),
    roll_n_papers_year = roll_sum3(n_papers_year),
    roll_enrichment = (roll_n / roll_n_papers_year) / corpus_rate,
    roll_ci_lower = wilson_lower_bound(roll_n, roll_n_papers_year) / corpus_rate,
    roll_ci_upper = wilson_upper_bound(roll_n, roll_n_papers_year) / corpus_rate
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| label: topics-over-time-count
#| fig-cap: "Papers per year, per topic. Faint bars: few papers that year."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 10
ggplot(topic_year_wilson, aes(x = publication_year, y = n, alpha = -ci_width)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#6a9870") +
  facet_wrap(~ topic, ncol = 4) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "", y = "Papers published that year", title = "Count") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
ggsave("topics_count_by_year.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 11, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### By year

```{r}
#| label: topics-over-time-enrichment
#| fig-cap: "Enrichment per year, per topic. Faint bars: few papers that year."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 10
ggplot(topic_year_wilson, aes(x = publication_year, y = enrichment, alpha = -ci_width)) +
  geom_col(fill = topic_col) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ topic, ncol = 4) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 4)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Enrichment vs. this topic's own corpus-wide rate", title = "Enrichment — by year") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
ggsave("topics_enrichment_by_year.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 11, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

#### Smoothed trend

```{r}
#| label: topics-over-time-enrichment-smoothed
#| fig-cap: "Same enrichment bars, with a 3-year rolling average and its own confidence band."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 10
ggplot(topic_year_roll, aes(x = publication_year)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = enrichment, alpha = -ci_width), fill = topic_col) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(roll_ci_lower, 0), ymax = pmin(roll_ci_upper, 4), group = topic),
              fill = trend_col, alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(aes(y = roll_enrichment, group = topic), colour = trend_col, linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ topic, ncol = 4) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 4)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Enrichment vs. this topic's own corpus-wide rate", title = "Enrichment — smoothed trend") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
ggsave("topics_enrichment_by_year_smoothed.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 11, height = 10, dpi = 300)
```

#### Table, by year

The numbers behind the count chart above and the By year chart: one row per topic and year. The interval is the Wilson 95% interval on the share of that year's papers.

```{r}
#| label: topics-over-time-table
#| classes: long-table
knitr::kable(
year_wilson_table(topic_year_wilson, "topic")
)
```

#### Table, smoothed

The numbers behind the Smoothed trend chart. Counts are pooled over a year and its neighbours (fewer at the ends of the range); the interval is computed on the pooled counts and divided by the topic's corpus rate, as plotted.

```{r}
#| label: topics-over-time-table-smoothed
#| classes: long-table
knitr::kable(
year_roll_table(topic_year_roll, "topic")
)
```

### Co-occurrence

```{r}
#| label: topics-cooccurrence-setup
topics <- df %>%
  select(contains("Topics")) %>%
  rename_with(~str_remove(., "Topics.."))
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Directional

```{r}
#| label: topics-cooccurrence-directional
#| fig-cap: "Directional: given a paper's Primary-coded topic (the facet), how often is each other topic marked Secondary on the same paper."
#| fig-width: 30
#| fig-height: 20
coocurrences <- c()
for(i in 1:nrow(topics)) {
  current_row <- topics[i, !is.na(topics[i,])]
  current_primaries <- names(current_row[which(current_row == "Primary")])
  current_secondaries <- names(current_row[which(current_row == "Secondary")])
  current_row <- paste(rep(current_secondaries, each = length(current_primaries)), current_primaries, sep = "_")
  coocurrences <- append(coocurrences, current_row)
}

coocdf <- data.frame(table(coocurrences)) %>%
  filter(substr(coocurrences, 1, 1) != "_") %>%
  separate_wider_delim(coocurrences, "_", names = c("Secondary", "Primary")) %>%
  mutate(Secondary = str_wrap(str_replace_all(Secondary, fixed("."), " "), width = 20)) %>%
  mutate(Primary = str_replace_all(Primary, fixed("."), " ")) %>%
  group_by(Primary) %>%
  mutate(Prop = Freq / sum(Freq))

ggplot(data = coocdf, aes(x = reorder_within(Secondary, Prop, Primary), y = Prop)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = topic_col) +
  facet_wrap(vars(Primary), scales = "free_x", nrow = 6) +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "")
```

#### Table, directional

The directional plot's numbers. One row per primary topic and secondary topic that occur together. A paper with several primaries or secondaries adds one pair for each combination, so pairs can exceed papers. The share is within the primary topic.

```{r}
#| label: topics-cooccurrence-directional-table
#| classes: long-table
knitr::kable(
coocdf %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Primary = str_squish(Primary), Secondary = str_squish(Secondary)) %>%
  arrange(Primary, desc(Freq), Secondary) %>%
  transmute(`Primary topic` = Primary, `Secondary topic` = Secondary, pairs = Freq,
            `share of the primary's pairs (%)` = as_pct(Prop))
)
```

#### Undirected

```{r}
#| label: topics-cooccurrence-undirected
#| fig-cap: "Undirected: which topics appear together at all, regardless of rank — present if either value is carried, pairing symmetric."
#| fig-width: 30
#| fig-height: 20
coocurrences_merged <- c()
for(i in 1:nrow(topics)) {
  current_row <- topics[i, !is.na(topics[i,])]
  current_present <- names(current_row)
  current_row <- paste(rep(current_present, each = length(current_present)), current_present, sep = "_")
  coocurrences_merged <- append(coocurrences_merged, current_row)
}

coocdf_merged <- data.frame(table(coocurrences_merged)) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(coocurrences_merged, "_", names = c("Topic.A", "Topic.B")) %>%
  filter(Topic.A != Topic.B) %>%
  mutate(Topic.A = str_wrap(str_replace_all(Topic.A, fixed("."), " "), width = 20)) %>%
  mutate(Topic.B = str_replace_all(Topic.B, fixed("."), " ")) %>%
  group_by(Topic.B) %>%
  mutate(Prop = Freq / sum(Freq))

ggplot(data = coocdf_merged, aes(x = reorder_within(Topic.A, Prop, Topic.B), y = Prop)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = topic_col) +
  facet_wrap(vars(Topic.B), scales = "free_x", nrow = 6) +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "")
```

#### Table, undirected

The undirected plot's numbers. Each pair appears twice, once under each topic as B, because the plot draws a panel for each. Papers is the number of papers carrying both, and the share is within B.

```{r}
#| label: topics-cooccurrence-undirected-table
#| classes: long-table
knitr::kable(
coocdf_merged %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Topic.A = str_squish(Topic.A), Topic.B = str_squish(Topic.B)) %>%
  arrange(Topic.B, desc(Freq), Topic.A) %>%
  transmute(`Topic B` = Topic.B, `Topic A` = Topic.A, papers = Freq,
            `share of B's pairs (%)` = as_pct(Prop))
)
```

### By first-author gender

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: topic-by-gender
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Proportion of papers by first-author gender, within each topic.
#|   Topics are labelled with their n; horizontal lines mark 25/50/75%
#|   for reference. Raw proportions, not corrected for the corpus-wide
#|   gender split.
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
topic_count_gender <- df %>%
  select(Authors..Genders..Author.1., contains("Topics")) %>%
  pivot_longer(!Authors..Genders..Author.1.,
               names_to = "topic",
               values_to = "count") %>%
  rename(gender_first_author = Authors..Genders..Author.1.)

merged_topic_gender <- topic_count_gender %>%
  filter(!is.na(count)) %>%
  mutate(topic = str_replace_all(str_remove(topic, "Topics.."), fixed("."), " ")) %>%
  count(topic, gender_first_author) %>%
  group_by(topic) %>%
  mutate(prop_merged = n / sum(n))

merged_topic_gender |>
  group_by(topic) |>
  mutate(ratio = n[gender_first_author == "Woman"] / sum(n),
         total = sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(topic = fct_reorder(topic, ratio),

  ggplot(aes(x = topic_label, y = prop_merged, fill = gender_first_author)) +

ggsave("topic_by_gender_merged.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

:::

### By full-author-list gender composition

Every paper's authors, sorted into one of five groups: solo female
author, solo male author, an all-female team, an all-male team, or a
mixed-gender team. Solo authorship is kept separate from team
composition — a single female author isn't the same thing as a team
that happens to be all women, and lumping them together would hide
that difference.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: composition-by-topic
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Proportion of papers by author-list gender composition (solo
#|   female/male, all-female/all-male team, mixed team), within each
#|   topic. Horizontal lines mark 25/50/75% for reference.
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
composition_topic <- composition_candidates %>%
  select(citekey, composition_singleauthor_split) %>%
  left_join(
    df %>% select(citekey, contains("Topics")) %>%
      pivot_longer(!citekey, names_to = "topic", values_to = "count") %>%
      filter(!is.na(count)) %>%
      mutate(topic = str_replace_all(str_remove(topic, "Topics.."), fixed("."), " ")),
    by = "citekey"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(topic), !is.na(composition_singleauthor_split))

comp_topic_summary <- composition_topic %>%
  count(topic, composition_singleauthor_split) %>%
  group_by(topic) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), total = sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

comp_topic_female_share <- comp_topic_summary %>%
  filter(composition_singleauthor_split %in% c("solo-female", "all-female (multi-author)")) %>%
  group_by(topic) %>%
  summarise(female_share = sum(prop), .groups = "drop")

comp_topic_summary %>%
  left_join(comp_topic_female_share, by = "topic") %>%
  mutate(female_share = replace_na(female_share, 0),
         topic = fct_reorder(topic, female_share),
         topic = fct_relabel(topic, ~str_wrap(., width = 25)),
         topic_label = paste0(topic, " (n=", total, ")"),
         topic_label = fct_reorder(topic_label, female_share),
         composition_singleauthor_split = factor(composition_singleauthor_split,
           levels = c("solo-female", "all-female (multi-author)", "mixed",
                      "all-male (multi-author)", "solo-male"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = topic_label, y = prop, fill = composition_singleauthor_split)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", linewidth = 0, width = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "solo-female" = "#bf616a", "all-female (multi-author)" = "#d89898",
    "mixed" = "#a0a8b8",
    "all-male (multi-author)" = "#8fbc8f", "solo-male" = "#4f6a31")) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Proportion", fill = NULL)
ggsave("composition_by_topic.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

#### Table

The plot's numbers, top row first. Each cell is the number of papers and its share of that topic's papers. "uncertain" gathers papers whose author list includes an uncertain gender; the plot draws them in grey.

```{r}
#| label: composition-by-topic-table
knitr::kable(
gender_composition_table(comp_topic_summary, comp_topic_female_share, "topic")
)
```

:::

### Mixed-gender authorship only

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: mixed-only-topic
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Each topic has two overlaid series on the same row, using different
#|   x-axes. Green dots (bottom axis): share of that topic's mixed-gender
#|   papers with a woman first author, dot size is the number of mixed
#|   papers behind that topic. Tan dots (top axis): every distinct
#|   author-team size found among that topic's mixed papers, dot size is
#|   how many papers have that size. Dashed vertical line marks 50% on
#|   the green (bottom) axis only.
#| fig-width: 11.5
#| fig-height: 9.5
mixed_topic_raw <- df %>%
  select(citekey, all_of(author_gender_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(author_gender_cols), names_to = "position", values_to = "gender") %>%
  mutate(gender = na_if(gender, "")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gender)) %>%
  mutate(author_n = as.integer(str_extract(position, "\\d+$"))) %>%
  arrange(citekey, author_n) %>%
  group_by(citekey) %>%
  summarise(n_authors = n(), n_women = sum(gender == "Woman"), n_men = sum(gender == "Man"),
            first = first(gender), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_women > 0, n_men > 0) %>%
  left_join(
    df %>% select(citekey, contains("Topics")) %>%
      pivot_longer(!citekey, names_to = "topic", values_to = "count") %>%
      filter(!is.na(count)) %>%
      mutate(topic = str_replace_all(str_remove(topic, "Topics.."), fixed("."), " ")),
    by = "citekey"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(topic)) %>%
  mutate(is_woman_first = as.numeric(first == "Woman"))

mixed_topic_summary <- mixed_topic_raw %>%
  group_by(topic) %>%
  summarise(prop = mean(is_woman_first), total = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(prop) %>%
  mutate(topic_label = paste0(str_wrap(topic, 22), " (n=", total, ")"),
         topic_label = factor(topic_label, levels = topic_label))

mixed_topic_teamsize_counts <- mixed_topic_raw %>%
  count(topic, n_authors, name = "n_at_size") %>%
  left_join(mixed_topic_summary %>% select(topic, topic_label), by = "topic")

mixed_topic_size_range <- range(mixed_topic_raw$n_authors)

ggplot() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey70", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = mixed_topic_teamsize_counts,
             aes(x = (n_authors - mixed_topic_size_range[1]) / diff(mixed_topic_size_range),
                 y = topic_label, size = n_at_size),
             colour = "#c8a87a", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = mixed_topic_summary, aes(x = prop, y = topic_label, size = total), colour = topic_col) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(-0.02, 1.02),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * diff(mixed_topic_size_range) + mixed_topic_size_range[1],
                         name = "Team size (tan)",
                         breaks = c(mixed_topic_size_range[1], 5, 10, 15, mixed_topic_size_range[2]))) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 8), name = "papers at\nthat size") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Share of mixed papers with a woman first author (green)", y = "")
ggsave("mixed_firstauthor_by_topic.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 11.5, height = 9.5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
               names_to = "method",

```

```{r}
  filter(!is.na(count)) %>%
  mutate(method = str_replace_all(str_remove(method, "Methods.."), fixed("."), " ")) %>%

ggplot(merged_count_method, aes(x = reorder(str_wrap(method, width = 25), n), y = n)) +
```

### Over time

```{r}
#| label: methods-over-time-setup
method_long_with_key <- df %>%
  select(citekey, publication_year, contains("Methods")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = contains("Methods"), names_to = "method", values_to = "count") %>%
  filter(!is.na(count)) %>%
  mutate(method = str_replace_all(str_remove(method, "Methods.."), fixed("."), " "))

method_corpus_rate <- method_long_with_key %>%
  distinct(citekey, method) %>%
  count(method, name = "n_corpus") %>%
  mutate(corpus_rate = n_corpus / n_total_papers)

method_year_wilson <- method_long_with_key %>%
  distinct(citekey, publication_year, method) %>%
  count(publication_year, method, name = "n") %>%
  complete(publication_year, method, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  left_join(n_per_year, by = "publication_year") %>%
  left_join(method_corpus_rate, by = "method") %>%
  mutate(
    prop = n / n_papers_year,
    enrichment = prop / corpus_rate,
    ci_lower = wilson_lower_bound(n, n_papers_year),
    ci_upper = wilson_upper_bound(n, n_papers_year),
    ci_width = ci_upper - ci_lower
  ) %>%
  arrange(method, publication_year)

method_year_roll <- method_year_wilson %>%
  arrange(method, publication_year) %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  mutate(
    roll_n = roll_sum3(n),
    roll_n_papers_year = roll_sum3(n_papers_year),
    roll_enrichment = (roll_n / roll_n_papers_year) / corpus_rate,
    roll_ci_lower = wilson_lower_bound(roll_n, roll_n_papers_year) / corpus_rate,
    roll_ci_upper = wilson_upper_bound(roll_n, roll_n_papers_year) / corpus_rate
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| label: methods-over-time-count
#| fig-cap: "Papers per year, per method. Faint bars: few papers that year."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8
ggplot(method_year_wilson, aes(x = publication_year, y = n, alpha = -ci_width)) +
  geom_col(fill = method_col) +
  facet_wrap(~ method, ncol = 4) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "", y = "Papers published that year", title = "Count") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
ggsave("methods_count_by_year.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 11, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### By year

```{r}
#| label: methods-over-time-enrichment
#| fig-cap: "Enrichment per year, per method. Faint bars: few papers that year."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8
ggplot(method_year_wilson, aes(x = publication_year, y = enrichment, alpha = -ci_width)) +
  geom_col(fill = method_col) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ method, ncol = 4) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 4)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Enrichment vs. this method's own corpus-wide rate", title = "Enrichment — by year") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
ggsave("methods_enrichment_by_year.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 11, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

#### Smoothed trend

```{r}
#| label: methods-over-time-enrichment-smoothed
#| fig-cap: "Same enrichment bars, with a 3-year rolling average and its own confidence band."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 8
ggplot(method_year_roll, aes(x = publication_year)) +
  geom_col(aes(y = enrichment, alpha = -ci_width), fill = method_col) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(roll_ci_lower, 0), ymax = pmin(roll_ci_upper, 4), group = method),
              fill = trend_col, alpha = 0.18) +
  geom_line(aes(y = roll_enrichment, group = method), colour = trend_col, linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ method, ncol = 4) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 4)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "Enrichment vs. this method's own corpus-wide rate", title = "Enrichment — smoothed trend") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
ggsave("methods_enrichment_by_year_smoothed.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 11, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

#### Table, by year

The numbers behind the count chart above and the By year chart: one row per method and year. The interval is the Wilson 95% interval on the share of that year's papers.

```{r}

#| classes: long-table
knitr::kable(
year_wilson_table(method_year_wilson, "method")
)
```

#### Table, smoothed

The numbers behind the Smoothed trend chart. Counts are pooled over a year and its neighbours (fewer at the ends of the range); the interval is computed on the pooled counts and divided by the method's corpus rate, as plotted.


### Co-occurrence

```{r}
#| label: methods-cooccurrence-setup
methods <- df %>%
  select(contains("Methods")) %>%
  rename_with(~str_remove(., "Methods.."))
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Directional

```{r}
#| label: methods-cooccurrence-directional
#| fig-cap: "Directional: given a paper's Primary-coded method (the facet), how often is each other method marked Secondary on the same paper."
#| fig-width: 20
#| fig-height: 20
coocurrences <- c()
for(i in 1:nrow(methods)) {
  current_row <- methods[i, !is.na(methods[i,])]
  current_primaries <- names(current_row[which(current_row == "Primary")])
  current_secondaries <- names(current_row[which(current_row == "Secondary")])
  current_row <- paste(rep(current_secondaries, each = length(current_primaries)), current_primaries, sep = "_")
  coocurrences <- append(coocurrences, current_row)
}

coocdf <- data.frame(table(coocurrences)) %>%
  filter(substr(coocurrences, 1, 1) != "_") %>%
  separate_wider_delim(coocurrences, "_", names = c("Secondary", "Primary")) %>%
  mutate(Secondary = str_wrap(str_replace_all(Secondary, fixed("."), " "), width = 20)) %>%
  mutate(Primary = str_replace_all(Primary, fixed("."), " ")) %>%
  group_by(Primary) %>%
  mutate(Prop = Freq / sum(Freq))

ggplot(data = coocdf, aes(x = reorder_within(Secondary, Prop, Primary), y = Prop)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = method_col) +
  facet_wrap(vars(Primary), scales = "free_x", nrow = 6) +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "")
```

#### Table, directional

The directional plot's numbers. One row per primary method and secondary method that occur together. A paper with several primaries or secondaries adds one pair for each combination, so pairs can exceed papers. The share is within the primary method.

```{r}
#| label: methods-cooccurrence-directional-table
#| classes: long-table
knitr::kable(
coocdf %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Primary = str_squish(Primary), Secondary = str_squish(Secondary)) %>%
  arrange(Primary, desc(Freq), Secondary) %>%
  transmute(`Primary method` = Primary, `Secondary method` = Secondary, pairs = Freq,
            `share of the primary's pairs (%)` = as_pct(Prop))
)
```

#### Undirected

```{r}
#| label: methods-cooccurrence-undirected
#| fig-cap: "Undirected: which methods appear together at all, regardless of rank — present if either value is carried, pairing symmetric."
#| fig-width: 20
#| fig-height: 20
coocurrences_merged <- c()
for(i in 1:nrow(methods)) {
  current_row <- methods[i, !is.na(methods[i,])]
  current_present <- names(current_row)
  current_row <- paste(rep(current_present, each = length(current_present)), current_present, sep = "_")
  coocurrences_merged <- append(coocurrences_merged, current_row)
}

coocdf_merged <- data.frame(table(coocurrences_merged)) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(coocurrences_merged, "_", names = c("Method.A", "Method.B")) %>%
  filter(Method.A != Method.B) %>%
  mutate(Method.A = str_wrap(str_replace_all(Method.A, fixed("."), " "), width = 20)) %>%
  mutate(Method.B = str_replace_all(Method.B, fixed("."), " ")) %>%
  group_by(Method.B) %>%
  mutate(Prop = Freq / sum(Freq))

ggplot(data = coocdf_merged, aes(x = reorder_within(Method.A, Prop, Method.B), y = Prop)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = method_col) +
  facet_wrap(vars(Method.B), scales = "free_x", nrow = 6) +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "")
```

#### Table, undirected

The undirected plot's numbers. Each pair appears twice, once under each method as B, because the plot draws a panel for each. Papers is the number of papers carrying both, and the share is within B.

```{r}
#| label: methods-cooccurrence-undirected-table
#| classes: long-table
knitr::kable(
coocdf_merged %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Method.A = str_squish(Method.A), Method.B = str_squish(Method.B)) %>%
  arrange(Method.B, desc(Freq), Method.A) %>%
  transmute(`Method B` = Method.B, `Method A` = Method.A, papers = Freq,
            `share of B's pairs (%)` = as_pct(Prop))
)
```

:::

### By first-author gender

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: method-by-gender
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Proportion of papers by first-author gender, within each method.
#|   Methods are labelled with their n; horizontal lines mark 25/50/75%
#|   for reference. Raw proportions, not corrected for the corpus-wide
#|   gender split.
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
method_count_gender <- df %>%
  select(Authors..Genders..Author.1., contains("Methods")) %>%

               names_to = "method",

merged_method_gender <- method_count_gender %>%

  count(method, gender_first_author) %>%

merged_method_gender |>
  group_by(method) |>
  mutate(ratio = n[gender_first_author == "Woman"] / sum(n),

  ggplot(aes(x = method_label, y = prop_merged, fill = gender_first_author)) +

ggsave("method_by_gender_merged.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

### By full-author-list gender composition

Every paper's authors, sorted into one of five groups: solo female
author, solo male author, an all-female team, an all-male team, or a
mixed-gender team. Solo authorship is kept separate from team
composition, so a single author's gender isn't treated as if it were
a team's composition.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: composition-by-method
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Proportion of papers by author-list gender composition (solo
#|   female/male, all-female/all-male team, mixed team), within each
#|   method. Horizontal lines mark 25/50/75% for reference.
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
composition_method <- composition_candidates %>%
  select(citekey, composition_singleauthor_split) %>%
  left_join(
    df %>% select(citekey, contains("Methods")) %>%
      pivot_longer(!citekey, names_to = "method", values_to = "count") %>%
      filter(!is.na(count)) %>%
      mutate(method = str_replace_all(str_remove(method, "Methods.."), fixed("."), " ")),
    by = "citekey"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(method), !is.na(composition_singleauthor_split))

comp_method_summary <- composition_method %>%
  count(method, composition_singleauthor_split) %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), total = sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

comp_method_female_share <- comp_method_summary %>%
  filter(composition_singleauthor_split %in% c("solo-female", "all-female (multi-author)")) %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(female_share = sum(prop), .groups = "drop")

comp_method_summary %>%
  left_join(comp_method_female_share, by = "method") %>%
  mutate(female_share = replace_na(female_share, 0),
         method = fct_reorder(method, female_share),
         method = fct_relabel(method, ~str_wrap(., width = 25)),
         method_label = paste0(method, " (n=", total, ")"),
         method_label = fct_reorder(method_label, female_share),
         composition_singleauthor_split = factor(composition_singleauthor_split,
           levels = c("solo-female", "all-female (multi-author)", "mixed",
                      "all-male (multi-author)", "solo-male"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = method_label, y = prop, fill = composition_singleauthor_split)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", linewidth = 0, width = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "solo-female" = "#bf616a", "all-female (multi-author)" = "#d89898",
    "mixed" = "#a0a8b8",
    "all-male (multi-author)" = "#8fbc8f", "solo-male" = "#4f6a31")) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Proportion", fill = NULL)
ggsave("composition_by_method.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```

#### Table

The plot's numbers, top row first. Each cell is the number of papers and its share of that method's papers. "uncertain" gathers papers whose author list includes an uncertain gender; the plot draws them in grey.

```{r}
#| label: composition-by-method-table
knitr::kable(
gender_composition_table(comp_method_summary, comp_method_female_share, "method")
)
```

:::

### Mixed-gender authorship only

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: mixed-only-method
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Each method has two overlaid series on the same row, using different
#|   x-axes. Navy dots (bottom axis): share of that method's mixed-gender
#|   papers with a woman first author, dot size is the number of mixed
#|   papers behind that method. Tan dots (top axis): every distinct
#|   author-team size found among that method's mixed papers, dot size is
#|   how many papers have that size. Dashed vertical line marks 50% on
#|   the navy (bottom) axis only.
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
mixed_method_raw <- df %>%
  select(citekey, all_of(author_gender_cols)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(author_gender_cols), names_to = "position", values_to = "gender") %>%
  mutate(gender = na_if(gender, "")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gender)) %>%
  mutate(author_n = as.integer(str_extract(position, "\\d+$"))) %>%
  arrange(citekey, author_n) %>%
  group_by(citekey) %>%
  summarise(n_authors = n(), n_women = sum(gender == "Woman"), n_men = sum(gender == "Man"),
            first = first(gender), .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_women > 0, n_men > 0) %>%
  left_join(
    df %>% select(citekey, contains("Methods")) %>%
      pivot_longer(!citekey, names_to = "method", values_to = "count") %>%
      filter(!is.na(count)) %>%
      mutate(method = str_replace_all(str_remove(method, "Methods.."), fixed("."), " ")),
    by = "citekey"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(method)) %>%
  mutate(is_woman_first = as.numeric(first == "Woman"))

mixed_method_summary <- mixed_method_raw %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarise(prop = mean(is_woman_first), total = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(prop) %>%
  mutate(method_label = paste0(str_wrap(method, 22), " (n=", total, ")"),
         method_label = factor(method_label, levels = method_label))

mixed_method_teamsize_counts <- mixed_method_raw %>%
  count(method, n_authors, name = "n_at_size") %>%
  left_join(mixed_method_summary %>% select(method, method_label), by = "method")

mixed_method_size_range <- range(mixed_method_raw$n_authors)

ggplot() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, colour = "grey70", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = mixed_method_teamsize_counts,
             aes(x = (n_authors - mixed_method_size_range[1]) / diff(mixed_method_size_range),
                 y = method_label, size = n_at_size),
             colour = "#c8a87a", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = mixed_method_summary, aes(x = prop, y = method_label, size = total), colour = method_col) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent, limits = c(-0.02, 1.02),
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * diff(mixed_method_size_range) + mixed_method_size_range[1],
                         name = "Team size (tan)",
                         breaks = c(mixed_method_size_range[1], 5, 10, 15, mixed_method_size_range[2]))) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(1.5, 8), name = "papers at\nthat size") +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "Share of mixed papers with a woman first author (navy)", y = "")
ggsave("mixed_firstauthor_by_method.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

#### Table

The plot's numbers, top row first. The interval is the Wilson 95% interval on the share of that method's mixed-gender papers with a woman first author. Team size is the number of authors per paper.

```{r}
#| label: mixed-only-method-table
knitr::kable(
gender_mixed_table(mixed_method_raw, "method")
)
```

### Over time

```{r}
#| label: sources-over-time-setup
source_long_with_key <- df %>%
  select(citekey, publication_year, contains("Sources.of.Evidence")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = contains("Sources.of.Evidence"), names_to = "source", values_to = "count") %>%
  filter(!is.na(count)) %>%

source_corpus_rate <- source_long_with_key %>%
  distinct(citekey, source) %>%
  count(source, name = "n_corpus") %>%
  mutate(corpus_rate = n_corpus / n_total_papers)

source_year_wilson <- source_long_with_key %>%
  distinct(citekey, publication_year, source) %>%
  count(publication_year, source, name = "n") %>%
  complete(publication_year, source, fill = list(n = 0)) %>%
  left_join(n_per_year, by = "publication_year") %>%
  left_join(source_corpus_rate, by = "source") %>%
  mutate(
    prop = n / n_papers_year,
    enrichment = prop / corpus_rate,
    ci_lower = wilson_lower_bound(n, n_papers_year),
    ci_upper = wilson_upper_bound(n, n_papers_year),
    ci_width = ci_upper - ci_lower
  ) %>%
  arrange(source, publication_year)

source_year_roll <- source_year_wilson %>%
  arrange(source, publication_year) %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  mutate(
    roll_n = roll_sum3(n),
    roll_n_papers_year = roll_sum3(n_papers_year),
    roll_enrichment = (roll_n / roll_n_papers_year) / corpus_rate,
    roll_ci_lower = wilson_lower_bound(roll_n, roll_n_papers_year) / corpus_rate,
    roll_ci_upper = wilson_upper_bound(roll_n, roll_n_papers_year) / corpus_rate
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| label: sources-over-time-count
#| fig-cap: "Papers per year, per source. Faint bars: few papers that year."
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 7
ggplot(source_year_wilson, aes(x = publication_year, y = n, alpha = -ci_width)) +
  geom_col(fill = source_col) +
  facet_wrap(~ source, ncol = 4) +
  scale_alpha_continuous(range = c(0.25, 1), guide = "none") +
  labs(x = "", y = "Papers published that year", title = "Count") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 8), axis.text.x = element_text(size = 6, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
ggsave("sources_count_by_year.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 11, height = 7, dpi = 300)
```

### Co-occurrence

```{r}
#| label: sources-cooccurrence-setup
sources <- df %>%
  select(contains("Sources.of.Evidence")) %>%
  rename_with(~str_remove(., "Sources.of.Evidence.."))
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Directional

```{r}
#| label: sources-cooccurrence-directional
#| fig-cap: "Directional: given a paper's Primary-coded source (the facet), how often is each other source marked Secondary on the same paper."
#| fig-width: 20
#| fig-height: 20
coocurrences <- c()
for(i in 1:nrow(sources)) {
  current_row <- sources[i, !is.na(sources[i,])]
  current_primaries <- names(current_row[which(current_row == "Primary")])
  current_secondaries <- names(current_row[which(current_row == "Secondary")])
  current_row <- paste(rep(current_secondaries, each = length(current_primaries)), current_primaries, sep = "_")
  coocurrences <- append(coocurrences, current_row)
}

coocdf <- data.frame(table(coocurrences)) %>%
  filter(substr(coocurrences, 1, 1) != "_") %>%
  separate_wider_delim(coocurrences, "_", names = c("Secondary", "Primary")) %>%
  mutate(Secondary = str_wrap(str_replace_all(Secondary, fixed("."), " "), width = 20)) %>%
  mutate(Primary = str_replace_all(Primary, fixed("."), " ")) %>%
  group_by(Primary) %>%
  mutate(Prop = Freq / sum(Freq))

ggplot(data = coocdf, aes(x = reorder_within(Secondary, Prop, Primary), y = Prop)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = source_col) +
  facet_wrap(vars(Primary), scales = "free_x", nrow = 6) +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "")
```

#### Table, directional

The directional plot's numbers. One row per primary source and secondary source that occur together. A paper with several primaries or secondaries adds one pair for each combination, so pairs can exceed papers. The share is within the primary source.

```{r}
#| label: sources-cooccurrence-directional-table
#| classes: long-table
knitr::kable(
coocdf %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Primary = str_squish(Primary), Secondary = str_squish(Secondary)) %>%
  arrange(Primary, desc(Freq), Secondary) %>%
  transmute(`Primary source` = Primary, `Secondary source` = Secondary, pairs = Freq,
            `share of the primary's pairs (%)` = as_pct(Prop))
)
```

#### Undirected

```{r}
#| label: sources-cooccurrence-undirected
#| fig-cap: "Undirected: which sources appear together at all, regardless of rank — present if either value is carried, pairing symmetric."
#| fig-width: 20
#| fig-height: 20
coocurrences_merged <- c()
for(i in 1:nrow(sources)) {
  current_row <- sources[i, !is.na(sources[i,])]
  current_present <- names(current_row)
  current_row <- paste(rep(current_present, each = length(current_present)), current_present, sep = "_")
  coocurrences_merged <- append(coocurrences_merged, current_row)
}

coocdf_merged <- data.frame(table(coocurrences_merged)) %>%
  separate_wider_delim(coocurrences_merged, "_", names = c("Source.A", "Source.B")) %>%
  filter(Source.A != Source.B) %>%
  mutate(Source.A = str_wrap(str_replace_all(Source.A, fixed("."), " "), width = 20)) %>%
  mutate(Source.B = str_replace_all(Source.B, fixed("."), " ")) %>%
  group_by(Source.B) %>%
  mutate(Prop = Freq / sum(Freq))

ggplot(data = coocdf_merged, aes(x = reorder_within(Source.A, Prop, Source.B), y = Prop)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = source_col) +
  facet_wrap(vars(Source.B), scales = "free_x", nrow = 6) +
  scale_x_reordered() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12, angle = 45, hjust = 1),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 14)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  labs(x = "", y = "")
```

#### Table, undirected

The undirected plot's numbers. Each pair appears twice, once under each source as B, because the plot draws a panel for each. Papers is the number of papers carrying both, and the share is within B.

```{r}

#| classes: long-table

coocdf_merged %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(Source.A = str_squish(Source.A), Source.B = str_squish(Source.B)) %>%
  arrange(Source.B, desc(Freq), Source.A) %>%
  transmute(`Source B` = Source.B, `Source A` = Source.A, papers = Freq,
            `share of B's pairs (%)` = as_pct(Prop))
)
```

### By full-author-list gender composition

Every paper's authors, sorted into one of five groups: solo female
author, solo male author, an all-female team, an all-male team, or a
mixed-gender team. Solo authorship is kept separate from team
composition, so a single author's gender isn't treated as if it were
a team's composition.

::: {.panel-tabset}

#### Plot

```{r}
#| label: composition-by-source
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Proportion of papers by author-list gender composition (solo
#|   female/male, all-female/all-male team, mixed team), within each
#|   source of evidence. Horizontal lines mark 25/50/75% for reference.
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 8
composition_source <- composition_candidates %>%
  select(citekey, composition_singleauthor_split) %>%
  left_join(
    df %>% select(citekey, contains("Sources.of.Evidence")) %>%
      pivot_longer(!citekey, names_to = "source", values_to = "count") %>%
      filter(!is.na(count)) %>%
      mutate(source = str_replace_all(str_remove(source, "Sources.of.Evidence.."), fixed("."), " ")),
    by = "citekey"
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(source), !is.na(composition_singleauthor_split))

comp_source_summary <- composition_source %>%
  count(source, composition_singleauthor_split) %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  mutate(prop = n / sum(n), total = sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup()

comp_source_female_share <- comp_source_summary %>%
  filter(composition_singleauthor_split %in% c("solo-female", "all-female (multi-author)")) %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarise(female_share = sum(prop), .groups = "drop")

comp_source_summary %>%
  left_join(comp_source_female_share, by = "source") %>%
  mutate(female_share = replace_na(female_share, 0),
         source = fct_reorder(source, female_share),
         source = fct_relabel(source, ~str_wrap(., width = 25)),
         source_label = paste0(source, " (n=", total, ")"),
         source_label = fct_reorder(source_label, female_share),
         composition_singleauthor_split = factor(composition_singleauthor_split,
           levels = c("solo-female", "all-female (multi-author)", "mixed",
                      "all-male (multi-author)", "solo-male"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = source_label, y = prop, fill = composition_singleauthor_split)) +
  geom_col(position = "fill", linewidth = 0, width = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75), colour = "black", linewidth = 0.4) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "solo-female" = "#bf616a", "all-female (multi-author)" = "#d89898",
    "mixed" = "#a0a8b8",
    "all-male (multi-author)" = "#8fbc8f", "solo-male" = "#4f6a31")) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Proportion", fill = NULL)
ggsave("composition_by_source.png", plot = last_plot(), width = 10, height = 8, dpi = 300)
```
